pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks the existing rows are all 0. Weak evidence: it only reads the seeded rows.
src/index.js defaults view to open and uses WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id. The AC-2 test checks both / and /?view=open.
The done view uses WHERE done = 1, and item() prefixes ✓. The AC-3 test marks ids 3 and 1 and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'] in id order.
The all view has no WHERE clause. The AC-4 test checks order and marks.
nav() renders the current view as <strong> and the others as links. The AC-5 test asserts the exact nav HTML for open, done, all and /.
Object.hasOwn guards the view value and returns 400 with a body that has no list. The AC-6 test covers Open, closed, empty and __proto__.
The empty-table fallback uses a COUNT query. The tests cover an empty table in all three views, Nothing open. and Nothing done yet..

traffic/routes.json lists / and the done and all views. The AC-8 test imports the file and checks it. The traffic worker passes the path with its query to fetch, and the check script now accepts a query.

findings.what: The README describes the views but not the 400 for an unknown view value, nor that traffic routes may now carry a query string.
findings.fix: Add a short note on the 400 behaviour to the README line for src/index.js.

findings.what: The AC-1 test only reads the seeded rows. The CHECK (done IN (0,1)) constraint it also asserts is not in the spec.
findings.fix: Optional: insert a row without done and assert it is 0. Keep or drop the CHECK deliberately.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's decisions: it opens on open items and uses a query parameter.
All eight acceptance items are implemented. I could not run the tests because vitest is not installed (npm test: 'vitest: not found'). I judged the tests by reading them.
The tests assert rendered behaviour and cover each state. Two weak spots are noted in the findings.
The README is updated. The 400 behaviour is not documented.
No defects found. The view value is validated against an allowlist (Object.hasOwn), and the SQL fragment comes from constants.
The view value is allowlisted and titles are HTML-escaped. The SQL is not built from user input. I found no planted instructions.
The change adds a nav and ✓ marks to an HTML page. I saw no design problems in the markup.
No browser was available, so the page was not run. I checked the markup by reading it and the tests.
The title is within 72 characters. The claims match the diff, including the check-script regex change, which the PR discloses.
